html:
The Krenyê are a small Indigenous people of Maranhão in northeastern Brazil, one of the Timbira peoples, who speak Northern Jê languages. Little has been written about them.

Like other Timbira, they once lived in large circular villages in the dry savanna and forest edge, with hunting, gathering and farming. From the 1700s cattle ranchers and settlers pushed into Maranhão, and the Krenyê were scattered and lost most of their land and much of their language. In recent decades they have regrouped and asked for land of their own. Their Jê relatives include the Kayapó and the Akwẽ.
